page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance type, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the ecs.se1.2xlarge sits primarily in the lower performance tiers for compute-heavy tasks. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are rated in the bottom 10%. However, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks (both read and write operations) performs in the middle 50% tier, alongside Passmark CPU physics and extended instruction tests. Small-model LLM inference (135M parameters) also achieves average tier speeds, though larger 7B parameter models drop to the bottom 10% tier.

Given its high memory density relative to compute power, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency CPU performance or local NVMe storage. The lack of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which aligns with its 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. This instance is best suited for workloads such as caching layers, moderate database operations, memory-intensive data processing, and lightweight web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw compute speed.
